column15: Morrison family (ex-Morrison Bowmore: Auchentoshan/Glen Garioch/Bowmore) craft distillery, founded 2017, own heritage Golden Promise barley; inaugural single malt scheduled for release March 2026. No peat/smoke level stated anywhere fetched (Wikipedia article is history-focused).

Isle of Lewis distillery (aka Red River distillery), operating since 2008; earliest release was 'Spirit of Lewis' before the current Abhainn Dearg-branded single malts. No peat/smoke level stated in Wikipedia's product list or the distillery's own site (fetched, JS-rendered, no extractable peat claim).

Distillery itself is never the bottling name: output is split into two differently-branded single-cask ranges, Man O' Words (unpeated, named for Robert Burns) and Man O' Sword (peated, named for Robert the Bruce) -- see those rows (parentSlug=annandale). peatProfile left unknown here since nothing is sold as plain 'Annandale'.
Annandale's single-cask range named after Robert Burns. Wikipedia states explicitly '(unpeated) Man O' Words'.

Annandale's single-cask range named after Robert the Bruce. Wikipedia states explicitly '(peated) Man O' Sword' but does not quantify intensity beyond the peated/unpeated split with Man O' Words, so classified medium rather than heavy pending a tasting-note source.

Source list marks this 'malt' but Wikipedia's Products section only documents Arbikie 1794 Highland Rye (Scotland's first commercial rye whisky in 100+ years) alongside gin/vodka -- no single malt is described -- so defaultTypeName left empty rather than forced to 'single malt' (range may span types / may not include a malt at all). No peat/smoke level stated anywhere fetched.

Original 1896 Ardgowan distillery in Greenock burned down in 1903 ('a river of flaming whisky'); modern distillery on Ardgowan Estate near Inverkip operating since 2016. No peat/smoke level found in the (history-focused) Wikipedia article.
Founded by master blender Andrew Rankin from 2015, ~GBP50m project, planning approved 2017. No peat/smoke level or distinct brand name found.
Archived whisky.com page quotes distillery manager Colin Poppy: the intended style 'is not smoky, but strong and expressive'. Scotland's first single-estate distillery (own barley, own maturation).
Official site (fetched) carries only marketing copy ('Nothing Wasted, Nothing Rushed, Nothing Ordinary'); no peat/smoke claim, and no Wikipedia article exists yet. Very new, obscure operation.

Archived whisky.com: 'The whiskies of Balmenach are rather fruity and not peated, which is very typical for a Speyside distillery... The malt of the Balmenach distillery is always unpeated.' scotchwhisky.com confirms Inver House has no plans to release it as a single malt at all -- almost everything on the market is via independent bottlers (Gordon & MacPhail, Douglas Laing).

Official site (fetched) describes a small-batch triple-distilled single malt/single cask project near Dumfries; founders 'one Scottish, one Irish' drawing on 'Irish and Scottish whisky making traditions' (triple distillation is an Irish-style choice, but no explicit peated/unpeated statement was made). No Wikipedia article; the site's own target opening was 2023, current status unconfirmed.

First spirit flowed June 2024; first bottling not expected until 2029. Wikipedia (Times, 2024) says production uses 'local peat and heather... in the process' alongside bere barley, but does not say this is peated malt/kilning versus some other use of peat, and the intended profile is described only as 'classically maritime'. Left unknown rather than guessing an intensity from that one ambiguous phrase -- flagged for reviewer to re-check once the whisky is actually released.

No Wikipedia article and no resolvable official website found (two plausible domains failed DNS resolution). Extremely new/obscure Falkirk-area project; nothing fetchable to cite. Alias kept brand-scoped only: 'blackness' is an ordinary English word.

Edinburgh-area Lowland distillery; per Wikipedia (Aug 2025) the range now includes both a 47% ABV non-peated spirit and a 51% ABV peated spirit, both matured in Muscat casks, with no separate brand name splitting the two (contrast Annandale's separately-named Man O'Sword / Man O'Words). Left as a single unknown-peat row for that reason rather than guessing which release a catalogue listing means.

First Scotch distillery in the Scottish Borders since 1837 (Hawick, opened 2018); also makes William Kerrs Gin (unrelated to whisky naming). No peat/smoke level stated in the (fully read) Wikipedia article. Alias kept brand-scoped: 'Borders' is a common geographic word.

Wikipedia: produced heavily peated whisky 1969-1973 (covering an Islay/Caol Ila shortfall), with most whisky made under the Brora name after 1973 in a 'lightly peated Highland style' before closure in 1983; reopened 2021 (still very young stock, no core range profile confirmed yet). scotchwhisky.com's whiskypedia entry: 'you will find Broras which are immensely oily and smoky, as well as some in which there is the merest exhalation of peat' -- i.e. genuinely variable by vintage. Classified medium as a defensible midpoint; a reviewer should treat individual releases as ranging from light to heavy.

No Wikipedia article. Guessed official domains for 'Deeside Brewery & Distillery' either failed TLS validation or resolved to an unrelated parked-domain sales page; the real site was not located this session. Nothing fetchable to cite.

The Cabrach Trust's site (fetched, redirects to cabrachtrust.org) is framed around the wider Cabrach heritage area rather than the distillery specifically; no distillery/whisky subpage or peat statement was found. No dedicated Wikipedia article exists (only the place 'Cabrach' and the distilleries list).

Built by Gordon & MacPhail near Grantown-on-Spey, operational since October 2022 (per the Gordon & MacPhail Wikipedia article). No dedicated Wikipedia article for the distillery itself; its own site (fetched) is a JS-rendered HubSpot page with no extractable peat statement, and other candidate sources either 403'd (whisky.com, masterofmalt) or had no dedicated article. Left unknown despite real effort -- no reason to assume unpeated Speyside style without a citation, especially since G&M's other distillery (Benromach) is deliberately peated.

Official site (fetched) markets 'multi-award winning spirits and liqueurs' with no whisky-specific peat statement. No dedicated Wikipedia article for the distillery (only a passing mention in the unrelated Kimbland distillery article, disputing which Orkney distillery matured whisky first).

Distillery's own releases are named 'Dornoch' (e.g. 'Dornoch 2017 3 Year Old Single Cask #001') under the umbrella 'Thompson Bros' label, which also carries independent bottlings of other distilleries -- see the separate 'thompson-bros' bottler row. No peat/smoke level stated in Wikipedia or the (JS-rendered) official site.

Retail label covering both Dornoch distillery's own output and independent bottlings of other distilleries (Wikipedia: 'products from the distillery, as well as independent bottlings from other distilleries, are released under the Thompson Bros brand name'). Added as a bonus row while researching Dornoch; no sample product names were available in this task to identify which other distilleries it bottles, so no further distillery rows were added for it here.

Bimber's Speyside outpost (floor maltings -- the first built at a Speyside distillery since 1898). Wikipedia states plainly: 'Dunphail make both peated and unpeated spirit' with no separate branding distinguishing the two, so left as a single unknown-peat row rather than guessing which a catalogue listing means (contrast Annandale's separately-named Man O'Sword / Man O'Words).
No dedicated Wikipedia article found (title guesses 404'd). Official site (fetched) markets St Andrews whisky tours/gin; its content is JS-rendered (Shopify) with no extractable peat statement.
Wikipedia states plainly: 'The distillery produces unpeated lowland style whisky.' First distillery to recommence production in the Falkirk area since Rosebank closed in 1993; operational since 2020.

Renamed from 'Crafty distillery' in 2025 on acquisition by actor Sam Heughan and Alex Norouzi (co-founders of the Sassenach spirits brand -- see the separate 'sassenach' blend row, deliberately not linked here by parentSlug given sourcing ambiguity). An earlier planned whisky brand name, 'Billy & Co.' (announced 2020), may or may not still apply after the 2025 rebrand -- not confirmed either way. No peat/smoke level stated anywhere fetched.

Consumer spirits brand co-founded by actor Sam Heughan (Outlander) and Alex Norouzi in 2021; Sassenach gin was contract-distilled at the Newton Stewart site since renamed Galloway Distillery (formerly Crafty distillery), and Wikipedia reports (Nov 2025) that Sassenach whisky and vodka production was being 'brought in-house' there too. Given the brand's history of contract/third-party sourcing, deliberately left unlinked to a specific distillery (no parentSlug, kind=blend not brand) rather than asserting single-origin -- a human reviewer should check whether current Sassenach whisky stock is entirely Galloway-distilled before promoting this to kind=brand with parentSlug=galloway.

SLUG REUSED from out/04/producer.tsv (identical distillery: this batch's gap-19 input line was the bare 'Glasgow' / Lowland / The Glasgow Distillery Company / malt). Row content copied from that batch's research so the merge deduplicates cleanly: re-opened 2014, first single malt distillery in Glasgow for 100+ years. Signature Range = The Original (unpeated) + Triple Distilled (unpeated) + The Peated -- see out/04/rule.tsv for the peated-expression rule (not re-added here to avoid a near-duplicate). Catalogue brand string is the bare number '1770'.

Output mostly goes into Diageo blends; official single-malt releases include a discontinued Flora and Fauna 12yo and Diageo's 2023 Singleton series (12/15/18yo), explicitly labelled Glendullan within the wider 'Singleton' range. Not aliasing bare 'Singleton', which is shared with the Dufftown and Glen Ord distilleries under the same umbrella brand and would mismatch them -- 'Glendullan' alone already matches 'The Singleton of Glendullan' as a substring. No peat/smoke level found in Wikipedia.

Wikipedia is explicit: 'The whisky from the Glengyle distillery is not called Glengyle, rather it is bottled under the name Kilkerran. This is because the name is owned by Loch Lomond Distillers, and used for their vatted malt.' peatProfile left unknown for this row since nothing is ever sold as plain 'Glengyle' -- see kilkerran (kind=brand, parentSlug=glengyle) for the actual product and its light peat profile. CONFLICT FOR REVIEWER: out/08/producer.tsv already has a 'kilkerran' row with kind=distillery, peatProfile unknown, and a same-named 'Heavily Peated' rule with no citation. This batch instead follows its own task brief and treats Kilkerran as kind=brand/parentSlug=glengyle (see that row), which is also now backed by a citation from the distillery's own site. Recommend keeping this batch's kilkerran row over 08's.

Distillery's own site, 12yo product page: 'Lightly peated and bottled at our standard bottling strength of 46% ABV, our Kilkerran 12 year old...'. The Heavily Peated limited release is a distinct, explicitly-named departure from this baseline -- see rule.tsv. SLUG COLLISION: see the note on the 'glengyle' row above -- out/08/producer.tsv already used slug 'kilkerran' for a kind=distillery row; this row deliberately reuses that same slug with kind=brand instead, per this task's explicit instructions. A human reviewer must reconcile the two.
Community/shareholder-owned Highland craft distillery (Dingwall, est. 2017); confirmed existence via Wikipedia but not researched in depth -- long-tail craft entry per this task's budget guidance.

SLUG REUSED from out/15/producer.tsv (identical distillery: this batch's gap-19 input line was 'Harris' / Islands / Isle of Harris Distillers Ltd. / malt). Single malt is The Hearach (first released autumn 2023) -- see the separate 'the-hearach' brand row added by this batch. Re-verified independently this session: Wikipedia states no peat/smoke level, and neither the distillery's own Hearach product page (fetched, Shopify age-gate, no extractable text) nor a launch-announcement article (fetched, no extractable text) yielded a citable claim. Left unknown, matching out/15's own conclusion.

Wikipedia: 'a single malt whisky called The Hearach, the Gaelic word for a resident of Harris'. No fetched source states a peat level (see the isle-of-harris row's note for the sources checked and their outcome); folklore among reviewers suggests lightly peated but this was deliberately not asserted without a citation. ALIAS NOTE: out/15/alias.tsv already maps 'The Hearach' directly to slug isle-of-harris (no separate brand row there); this batch instead creates a dedicated kind=brand row per its task instructions, so 'The Hearach' now aliases to two different slugs across batches -- a human reviewer must pick one (recommend keeping this brand-row version for consistency with the Glengyle/Kilkerran pattern).

Edinburgh Lowland distillery; first single malt 'Arrival' released Oct 2023, followed by a three-strong 'Founding Series' (Embra, peated; Ambir, specialty malts; Pitch, speciality yeast) -- see the separate 'embra' brand row. No source states a peat level for Arrival or the base range itself, only that Embra specifically is peated, so left unknown here rather than assumed unpeated by contrast.

Part of Holyrood's 2024-25 'Founding Series' of three single malts. Wikipedia: 'Embra, a peated whisky' -- stated without further qualifying intensity, so classified medium rather than heavy pending a tasting-note source.
Fife Lowland distillery (John Fergus & Co.); long-tail craft entry, not researched in depth per this task's budget guidance.
RAER Spirits' Lowland distillery near East Kilbride; long-tail craft entry, not researched in depth per this task's budget guidance.
